chunks: And by this chain, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'There happen to be three shirts for me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' So he did not cease (numbering) until it reached ten. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do they not make each other last longer?' I said, 'Yes, and were I to wear one, it would last for a little (while).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.يُوَدِّعُ: to leave behind / preserve by rotation

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on owning multiple sets of clothing?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the upper limit of permissible clothing ownership, resolving the tension between modesty and practical preservation. The Imam’s reasoning highlights that maintaining multiple garments ensures longevity through rotation, a practical consideration that validates ownership beyond a single item without implying extravagance. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of *islah* (preservation) as a valid justification for retaining multiple sets of essential attire.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There happen to be three shirts for me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. So he did not cease (numbering) until it reached ten. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do they not make each other last longer?’ I said, ‘Yes, and were I to wear one, it would last for a little (while)’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 11. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if I can have three shirts. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’ I asked again until I reached ten shirts and he (the Imam) said, ‘Does exchanging give them more durability?’ I said, ‘It does, were I to wear one of them for a longer time, it would become less durable.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
